file_roles.evidence: parseDate's early return did not recognise the value the report gives: 'if (text == null || text.isEmpty())' becomes 'if (text == null || text.isEmpty() || "D:".equals(text.trim()))'. The exception is raised inside that same method, 'at org.apache.pdfbox.util.DateConverter.parseDate(DateConverter.java:656)', so the code that walked past the end of "D:   " is the defect, and no other source file was changed.

rationale: The trace is three frames deep and only one of them is project-owned: 'at org.apache.pdfbox.util.DateConverter.parseDate(DateConverter.java:656)' called from 'DateConverter.toCalendar(DateConverter.java:724)', above it only java.lang.String.charAt and StringLatin1.charAt. The fix adds the missing case to the same method's guard, '"D:".equals(text.trim())', which is exactly the input the report quotes. Cause, symptom and the single gold file are the same method.
notes: REPORT-NAMES-FIX: the report quotes the triggering value, 'Happens with "D:   " as a date.', the trace names the method and line, and the adopted fix hard-codes that value. Convention applied: adding a check for a legal-but-unhandled input is causal when the changed file owns the feature and nothing elsewhere was treated as broken (HIVE-2334, KAFKA-6250 group). The commit message, 'PDFBOX-5046: catch more empty dates', describes the same thing the hunk shows. The fix touched 2 files and only 1 is gold, so the test file was filtered as intended.
